Modern Tiny House Ventura Is Bright, Spacious, and Equipped for Family Life
23 photos
Photo: Mint Tiny House Company
While some downsizers love rustic tiny homes that resemble traditional mountain cabins, others prefer more modern designs with sleek, darker exteriors and warm, bright interiors. The Ventura tiny house falls into the latter category, combining contemporary styling with a generous footprint and all the amenities of a conventional home.
Ventura is a brand new tiny home on wheels from the Mint Tiny House Company, a prominent North American builder based in British Columbia, and is one of those designs that prove smaller dimensions shouldn’t get in the way of comfort and style. It measures 40 feet (12.2 meters) long and offers a spacious layout that sleeps up to eight people, which makes it a great option for families or those who want flexible spaces for different activities or accommodating guests.
Built on a quad-axle trailer, the Ventura is also wider than standard tiny houses on wheels. It has a width of 10 feet (3 meters), which means it requires a special permit to be towed on public roads, but its oversized dimensions result in considerably more room for all the amenities needed for modern living.
Designed to melt into its surroundings and remain unassuming, this house on wheels boasts an elegant exterior clad in muted black engineered wood and dotted with large windows all around. The glazing is more than a decorative feature, as the numerous windows and two glass doors help create a very luminous and airy ambiance inside, while also giving dwellers attractive views of their surroundings.
Photo: Mint Tiny House Company/ Kerry Tarnow on YouTube Indeed, once you step inside, you’ll be impressed by how spacious it feels. The interior offers 520 square feet (48 square meters) of interior space, including its lofts, and the floor plan includes separate living and sleeping areas, a fully equipped kitchen, a dedicated dining space, a bathroom, and even a laundry. Storage is also abundant and every area is meticulously designed to feel welcoming, proving that downsizing doesn’t necessarily mean giving up the comforts of a conventional home.
Mint Tiny House used a mix of natural materials to give the living space warmth and serenity. Stained wood planks were used to cover the ceiling and a feature wall behind the living room sofa, while the remaining walls are finished in V-groove plywood. Vinyl plank flooring runs throughout the house, while the kitchen cabinetry is made of high-quality laminate and paired with elegant quartz countertops. Everything looks modern and functional, achieving a clean, minimalist aesthetic.
But the most prominent feature that sets Ventura apart is the abundance of windows in conjunction with glass entrances. Thanks to them, the home’s interior feels much more spacious and welcoming. This is particularly notable downstairs, where an open-plan configuration brings the kitchen, dining, and living areas together. This entire space is bathed in natural light and opens to the outdoors in the best way, offering great views.
Photo: Mint Tiny House Company/ Kerry Tarnow on YouTube The kitchen is located at one end of the house, leaving the center open for dining, gathering, and socializing. It has an L-shape configuration and is designed as a proper cooking space, with oodles of low and upper cabinets, ample counters pace, and practical appliances.
It comes equipped with a fridge/freezer, an oven, a three-burner gas cooktop, and a stainless steel sink. A dishwasher, one of the appliances considered a luxury in tiny homes, is also included. A separate dining table with three chairs sit under a large window, creating a dedicated place to eat.
The adjacent living room is set up with a convertible couch that is strategically placed to make the most of the vistas. There are windows on either side of a full wall section that is wired for an entertainment center. The sofa extends into a bed for two people, offering extra sleeping space for guests.
Ventura is meant to comfortably accommodate up to eight people in total, and its clever layout makes it possible without feeling cramped. It features two easy-to-access loft bedrooms, as well as a ground-floor bedroom.
Photo: Mint Tiny House Company/ Kerry Tarnow on YouTube This main bedroom is situated at the end of the trailer and is completely separated from the rest of the house, enclosed behind a sliding door. It features a double bed and built-in wardrobes (if you opt for them) and offers plenty of headroom and space to move around comfortably. But what makes it more appealing is a set of double glass doors that open directly to the outdoors, turning it into a cozy sanctuary connected to the surroundings.
A single staircase leads up to the two lofts, showcasing yet again the cleverness of this floor plan. It doesn’t take up much space from the ground level and comes with integrated storage inside the first two steps. Once you reach the upper level, the space branches in two directions. On one side is a larger loft with another double bed, while the other side contains a smaller loft, also configured as additional sleeping space. The latter is open to the area below, with a wooden railing for protection.
Photo: Mint Tiny House Company/ Kerry Tarnow on YouTube With this configuration featuring four sleeping areas, the Ventura tiny house should appeal to larger families or anyone who regularly hosts overnight guests. However, the two lofts offer flexibility, and owners can use them for various purposes, from reading nooks and extra lounging areas to storage space.
Moving back downstairs, on the narrow corridor leading to the main bedroom there are two more doors. Behind the first one, we discover the bathroom, which follows the same design language as the kitchen, with matching cabinets and quartz surfaces, and includes a sink, a toilet, and a walk-in shower.
Photo: Mint Tiny House Company/ Kerry Tarnow on YouTube Next door is a dedicated laundry area. Although it’s not a full utility room but rather a laundry closet that houses a stacked washer and dryer, but it still gives dwellers the convenience of doing laundry at home.
The only thing left to discuss is pricing. The Ventura tiny house is available for a base price of CAD $179,750 in Canada, which is about USD$129,750, but the final price is, of course, dictated by the chosen configuration and options. The Mint Tiny House Company notes that the twin-loft configuration is only available in the United States. A first look at this spacious tiny home is available in the video below.

By Rainbow Nelson
21 October 2026
In the seven years since TOC Americas last took place in Cartagena, global laden container volumes have slipped about 10% below where they would have been without the multiple disruptions that have hit the industry since 2018, according to Dinesh Sharma, director at Drewry Maritime Advisors.
Sharma’s research measured growth from 2018 against forecasts of where the industry had imagined it would be today last time they met in Cartagena. Predicting the future, he said, was and is not easy. Transshipment hubs grew by about 6% a year on average over that period, against roughly 3% for gateway ports and 1.5% for the underlying economies they serve. The inefficiency, he said, is no longer contained at the big transshipment hubs: it is flowing through to gateways too, leaving Latin America’s overall throughput an estimated 2–3% below his 2018 projection. Performance varies sharply by market, Sharma added: Mexico and Brazil are growing more slowly, while Colombia is seeing strong consumer spending and rising real wages, with Peru, Chile and Ecuador following a similar pattern.
Offering a geopolitical insight into the direction of travel, Henry Ziemer, of the Centre for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) in Washington, said the current political situation only further complicated the commercial picture. Ziemer argued the Americas are becoming strategically important precisely because the rest of the world has become more violently contested. “I think the Americas are becoming a key hedge, geopolitical hedge, in a more contentious world,” he said.
A tug of war over ownership
That attention, Ziemer said, is not without cost. Washington’s growing interest in the region’s infrastructure raises the odds that port decisions get caught up in politics rather than commercial logic. “Who controls ports and maritime infrastructure matters now more than ever,” he said, warning that US agencies do not always have full visibility of who actually owns or runs a given facility. “Ports can sometimes be caught in a bit of a tug of war where different agencies are acting under imperfect information about ownership structures, about operational control,” he said.
Who wins Panama’s next tenders
Ziemer’s clearest example was Panama, which is running caretaker arrangements at Balboa and Cristóbal through APM Terminals and TiL while preparing to tender two new ports. “There’s an expectation from the administration in the United States that a U.S. company will be basically receiving one of those ports,” he said. He questioned whether that expectation matches the market: “Will they be the most competitive option? Will they adhere to the specifications that the Panamanian government is looking for?” For Ziemer, that is the sharper risk, not the cost of capital. “The real dilemma is not so much in the financing side, but in the question of which countries and which companies are delivering the infrastructure capability,” he said.
Reading the money, not the flags
Other panelists read the same uncertainty in more commercial terms. Natalia Gil, economic investigations leader at Grupo Puerto de Cartagena (GPC), told the panel that capacity figures increasingly conceal differences in connectivity and reliability. Her team’s analysis of routes across the Caribbean and Panama between 2023 and 2026 found that a container line changes a route, a service or a parameter of a service on average every 3.9 days, with the toughest quarters for Cartagena, including the Panama Canal drought and disruption around the Strait of Hormuz and the Suez Canal, also the quarters when the port won the most new services.
Nicolas Romero, regional head Latin America at Pacific International Lines (PIL), said the line is redesigning its ships around the region’s constraints rather than waiting for ports to catch up: “we take the challenge to adapt the fleet to the needs of the terminal.” Enrique Piqueras, chief executive of PSA Panama, argued the bigger bottleneck in most Latin American countries sits outside the terminal gate altogether, a problem he said he had seen repeat in Peru, Colombia, Argentina and Panama. “Competitiveness isn’t given by the port … it’s given by the environment,” he said.
Asked by an audience member from the Panama Canal Authority how to read where geopolitics is heading, Ziemer pointed away from announcements and towards capital flows, and towards countries with existing ties to Washington such as Panama, Colombia and Mexico. Sharma agreed the political backdrop was real, whoever occupies the White House. “As much as you like the current administration or dislike the current administration, what this has resulted is in a great big shakeup,” he said, pointing to a shift from integrated tariff structures towards shorter-lived bilateral trade frameworks that add short-haul volume to ports without necessarily adding profit. But asked where capital was actually landing, he pointed to his own data rather than Washington’s intentions: “If we just look at the expansions happening within Latin America, the vast majority of them are brownfield expansions.”
The gap between the two readings showed again when Sharma was pressed on how he weighs geopolitics against his own projections. “We just take what Henry says and we convert them into numbers,” he said.

Incrementum gold fund manager Ronald-Peter Stöferle chats with TNM Western Editor Henry Lazenby during the Mining Forum Americas in Colorado Springs.
Posted By: Henry Lazenby October 21, 2026
Liechtenstein-based Incrementum gold fund manager Ronald-Peter Stöferle sees bargains in mining shares after gold’s pullback, even as his active gold strategy holds almost 40% cash.
The strategy’s investment signal turned defensive earlier this year, Stöferle told The Northern Miner late last month at the Mining Forum Americas in Colorado Springs. Yet meetings with mining executives left him encouraged by their restraint on acquisitions and new projects, suggesting producers are maintaining spending discipline as earnings rise.
“It doesn’t mean that they won’t screw it up at some point in the cycle,” he told The Miner’s Western Editor, Henry Lazenby. “But I think now it’s kind of the sweet spot that we’re seeing in the mining space.”
For miners, the opportunity is to attract investors who have overlooked the sector. Stöferle sees investors with broader mandates gradually warming to gold exposure, potentially widening the pool of capital available.

Honda Takes Aim at New Riders with Brand-New CBR500R Four Supersport Bike
26 photos
Photo: Honda
In the very rich offering of Honda motorcycles, there is this category the Japanese call the Super Sport (alternatively spelled Supersport). It is the segment that includes, for instance, the CBR600RR, CBR1000RR, or the mighty CBR1000RR-R Fireblade SP.
All these bikes need quite a bit of experience from whoever wants to ride them, so not exactly noob friendly. Knowing this, the Japanese bike maker decided to expand the range with something called the CBR500R Four.
Situated at the opposite end from the Fireblade SP, it has been developed as a sort of offshoot of the CB400 Super Four, which has been selling in Japan for more than three decades, but one that’s new from top to bottom. And on top of that, it packs all the most modern technologies Honda presently has access to.
The 2027 Honda CBR500R Four, as it will be known from now on, is built around a steel diamond frame supported by an aluminum swingarm and a KYB suspension system that relies on 41 mm USD forks at the front and a Pro-Link rear shock.
Inside the frame, Honda installed a brand-new 500cc inline four-cylinder engine, which is not exactly a monster when it comes to output. Then again, this motorcycle is aimed squarely at new riders, both to the world of motorcycling and to Honda, so the numbers below should be more than enough: 69 hp and 46 Nm of torque, with the redline arriving at 12,500 rpm.
The engine and its power delivery are controlled by means of a six-speed transmission that can be run through the E-Clutch system, allowing for clutchless starts, stops, and gear changes. That should work wonders for A2 license holders, who will be treated to a properly detuned version.
The new middleweight bike rides on 17-inch wheels shod in Pirelli Diablo Rosso tires, which are also fitted with Nissin braking hardware. Riders also have access to three riding modes and two user modes, controlled by means of the five-inch screen at the front.
Honda did not say specifically when the new motorcycle will hit the market, but it already revealed that there will be two color choices on the table, namely the Ignition Red (Tricolour) and the Mat Ballistic Black Metallic.
Pricing for the machine varies depending on the European country it sells in (and to learn more about that, you should get in touch with your local dealer), but no matter where that is, the 2027 Honda CBR500R Four throws in, as standard, a twin LED projector and a front fairing connected to the tank and side panels.
We have no word on whether Honda plans to launch the new motorcycle on the American market, where the entry-level position is presently occupied by the CBR600RR in this segment.

Ontario Midland Railroad has secured an $11.2 million federal grant to rehabilitate approximately 10 miles of track in Wayne County, New York, improving infrastructure that supports the region’s agricultural and manufacturing shippers.
The Wayne County Mainline Safety and Reliability Project will replace approximately nine miles of rail, resurface eight grade crossings, replace seven turnouts and remove three others. Work also includes ballast placement, tamping and track surfacing, according to an Oct. 19 announcement from the railroad and U.S. Sens. Chuck Schumer and Kirsten Gillibrand.
The award comes through the Federal Railroad Administration ’s Consolidated Rail Infrastructure and Safety Improvements, or CRISI, program. The project is intended to modernize deteriorating infrastructure, improve freight transportation efficiency and support economic development.
“This funding will support comprehensive modernization of Ontario Midland Railroad’s east-west corridor by replacing aging infrastructure with new rail and crossties,” Wayne County Economic Development and Planning Executive Director Brian Pincelli said in the announcement.
Ontario Midland provides local freight service across Wayne and Monroe counties, including the eastern Rochester metropolitan area, and interchanges with CSX at Newark. The railroad has served the region since 1979.
“We are profoundly grateful to Senators Schumer and Gillibrand for their relentless advocacy and partnership in securing this critical 2025–2026 grant for the Ontario Midland Railroad,” said Ontario Midland Chairman Robert Babcock and President Jeffrey Bauman, in a joint statement. “This federal support is a game-changer for our operations, ensuring we can maintain safe, reliable service and continue driving economic growth across the communities we proudly serve.”
The grant is part of a combined $20.8 million in CRISI funding announced for Ontario Midland and Falls Road Railroad. Falls Road received approximately $9.6 million to rehabilitate rail infrastructure along about 40 miles between Brockport and Lockport, including rail and tie replacement, bridge rehabilitation and resurfacing of six grade crossings.
The investments will help strengthen regional supply chains, reduce truck traffic and fuel consumption, and support businesses that depend on freight rail, the senators said.

To understand why captives and alternative risk structures are drawing so much attention from fleets right now, it helps to start with an uncomfortable fact about the insurance industry itself: commercial auto liability hasn’t been profitable on an underwriting basis since 2010, when the loss ratio came in at 97.1%. That’s a razor-thin 2.9% margin .
So how do insurance companies stay in business? Frank Kneeland, Senior Vice President of Sales at Reliance Partners , says the answer has less to do with underwriting than most fleet owners realize.
“Most of these insurers are essentially massive banks or investment firms,” Kneeland said. “They’re investing the premium dollars they collect, which is part of why many require a finance agreement or payment in full. They want that money working for them as soon as possible. That’s how they turn a profit even in a bad underwriting year.”
Captive and alternative risk structures are designed to change that dynamic. Rather than handing premium dollars to a traditional insurer and hoping for the best, a fleet that joins a captive retains more responsibility for its own losses. In exchange, the fleet shares in the financial results of the program.
“You’re returning the underwriting profit, the unspent premium, and the investment income that accrued over the term back to the fleet instead of the insurer,” Kneeland said.
According to Kneeland, this has a massive effect on the entire interplay between a fleet and its broker. “It changes the conversation from simply comparing premiums to looking at the fleet’s total cost of risk: claims, expenses, reinsurance, performance, all of it,” Kneeland said.
That, in turn, changes what a broker actually needs to understand about a client’s operation.
“We have to understand how the fleet operates, how claims are handled, and whether its leadership is prepared to manage risk over the long term,” Kneeland said. “A captive can create more control and more upside, but it also requires engagement and discipline.”
Explained simply, a captive gives a fleet a more active role in funding its own insurance losses. In the standard market, performance is pooled whether a company likes it or not.
“Everyone in the standard market is affected if the larger group of insureds performs poorly. Even the best operators running clean can see an increase because of everyone else in the pool,” Kneeland said. “Generally, the bottom 30% of performers end up offsetting everyone else, because auto claims can be so large.”
A group captive narrows that pool dramatically. “When you enter a group captive, you’re shrinking the group down to a very limited pool of best-in-class operators,” Kneeland said. “You’re cutting off the members who were dragging down the standard market the most, while allowing everyone left to share in the underwriting profit and keep rates stable year over year.”
That stability, Kneeland said, draws in the fleets who ultimately become strong candidates. It inherently appeals safety-focused operators who feel like they’ve been subsidizing worse performers for years.
Even among brokers, Kneeland said, there’s a persistent misunderstanding about what a captive actually promises.
“The goal isn’t really about hoping to share in some theoretical underwriting profit,” Kneeland said. “In reality, you’re retaining a higher level of risk, making the interest on your insurance dollars work for you instead of the insurer, and building a claims team you can actually hire and fire as needed. That’s something you never had that level of control over in the standard market.”
The predictability is just as vital as the cost. One of the biggest goals of a captive program is a renewal that fleets can plan around, rather than the kind of blindside still common in the standard market. Many carriers give no indication that anything unusual is coming, then deliver a massive increase just days before the policy renews. A surprise like that can be devastating to a fleet, especially given the thin margins and bottlenecked cash flow that characterize the industry.
Control extends well beyond the balance sheet. Kneeland points to the connection between safety performance and insurance outcomes as one of the most underappreciated benefits of moving into a captive.
“In the standard market, a fleet may feel like its investment in safety isn’t reflected in its pricing,” Kneeland said. “In a captive, members have much more visibility into the program’s losses.”
The advantages apply to a lot more than cost control, too. Fleets that make the move also gain better access to claims data, more active loss-control support, and a longer-term view of their own risk profile.
If your fleet is exploring a captive for the first time, Kneeland breaks the process into three stages: discovery, quoting, and timing.
Discovery starts with understanding a fleet’s operations, current program, financial capacity, and goals, followed by a review of loss history and standard underwriting information to determine whether the risk is even suitable for the structure. From there, the quoting process involves underwriting, actuarial analysis, a review of the captive’s rules and financials, collateral requirements, and working through reinsurance and fronting arrangements.
How long that takes depends heavily on the path. “If a fleet is joining an established group captive, the process may take a few months, depending on how quickly we’re able to get the necessary information,” Kneeland said. “A new program or structure can take considerably longer.”
Timing the start of that process matters just as much as the process itself.
“I like to start this mid-term rather than trying to line it up with the renewal date,” Kneeland said. “This is a more complex product, and clients join because of the benefits it provides, but there’s generally more up-front cost because of collateral requirements. Not being boxed in by a deadline lets the company really learn and understand the commitment before the pressure of a renewal is bearing down on them.”
If there’s one blind spot Kneeland keeps running into, it’s a fixation on premium at the expense of everything else. “Total cost of risk — that’s the piece so many fleets miss, because they’re so focused on the premium number that they don’t look at the full picture,” he said.
The full picture includes losses retained through deductibles, funding collateral, and the expenses that come with absorbing claims.
Kneeland sees one trend in particular gaining traction for the wrong reasons: Risk Retention Groups.
“These are a hugely important part of the conversation right now,” Kneeland said. “A lot of these have incredibly weak financials, an enormous number of exclusions, and no backing from any state guaranty fund.”
Saving a small amount on premium can be a poor decision if a fleet hasn’t actually evaluated the program.
“The right comparison isn’t one premium against another,” Kneeland said. “It’s the full cost, the protection being provided, and how the structure fits the fleet’s risk and financial capacity.”
Why Now
The trucking insurance market’s volatility over the past several years hasn’t gone unnoticed, and Kneeland sees a direct line between that volatility and the growing interest in alternative risk. “When the traditional market gets volatile, fleets start asking whether there are other ways to finance risk and gain more control over their insurance costs,” he said. “Alternative risk structures give qualified fleets a way to take a longer-term view and connect their own performance more directly to their insurance results.”
What’s the underlying cause? “Honestly, I just think the traditional market is such a mess right now that more companies than ever are trying to find ways to control their costs and get rewarded more fairly for their safety efforts,” Kneeland said.
Getting Started
If you’re a fleet owner or manager and you’re sitting on the fence, Kneeland’s advice starts before any underwriting data gets pulled together.
“Have a very honest conversation about your fleet’s current safety program and your overall cost of risk,” he said. “Without a strong safety program, this isn’t going to be the right fit.”
From there, timing becomes the central issue again. “We have to start these conversations early, so the fleet actually understands its options,” Kneeland said. “We don’t want to start this a month before renewal and expect results. Most brokers don’t even present this option or explain it the right way, so education and really understanding the risk matter enormously.”
And for fleets that wait too long to have that conversation, Kneeland said the cost is easy to overlook because it’s invisible. “If you’re a best-in-class operator paying standard market rates with practically no claims, you’re losing underwriting profit, losing the investment income on your own premium, and you’re probably still getting rate increases anyway.”
If you want to dig deeper into captives and alternative risk, you can follow Kneeland’s weekly breakdowns on LinkedIn , where he regularly unpacks these structures for the trucking industry.

WildAx Mercury Is a Tiny Motorhome That Still Makes Room for Everything
14 photos
Photo: WildAx
What's small enough to fit inside any parking spot but large enough to be comfortable to live in even for longer stretches? Don't answer that, because we already have the answer: it's the brand-new 2027 WildAx Mercury motorhome.
WildAx is a UK-based manufacturer of campervans and motorhomes that specializes in high-spec hand-crafted RVs on chassis from Fiat, Ford, MAN, and Citroen. For 2027, their focus is on convenience and (relative) affordability, with a conversion that delivers the mightiest punch in the most surprising package.
Mercury debuted at the 2026 edition of the Motorhome & Caravan Show at NEC Birmingham, but WildAx introduced it online prior to that, as you can see in the video tour at the bottom of the page. This is a couple's RV, designed with maximum convenience in mind, both when out of the city and inside it, so it's small when you need it but still big enough to have everything included.
And I do mean "everything." Where most motorhomes of this size (campervans) will sacrifice kitchen facilities or the entire bathroom, or will have you convert the dining space into a bed at night, Mercury is able to sidestep all these and present itself as a complete solution.
Photo: WildAx It's still cramped because of its compact dimensions, but that's the whole point because you will need it to remain nimble on city streets and fit inside all parking spots. For the first time in several years, we're witnessing a return to basics in terms of the size of available RV solutions in Europe, and the Mercury is a good example of that.
Built on the new Ford Transit chassis and offered standard with 130 hp on the engine and six-speed manual transmission, the Mercury comes in at just 5.4 meters (17.7 feet) of total length and 2.05 meters (6.7 feet) of width. This is a high-top model, so overall height is 2.8 meters (9.18 feet), compensating a bit for the otherwise very compact dimensions.
At this size, Mercury is tiny even for the European market, let alone by U.S. standards. Over in Europe, the smallest van conversions offered in series production are at least 6 meters (19.6 feet) long, and many manufacturers have considered 7 meters (23 feet) a more suitable length to be working with in recent years. As I said, we're going back to the basics, but in a way that won't feel like a total compromise.
Photo: WildAx In order to fit everything you need inside the Mercury, WildAx rethinks the "standard" campervan layout. They add a small but complete and wet bathroom behind the driver's seat, the single-block kitchen across the way, a fridge with a wardrobe next to the bathroom, and the lounge at the rear.
For the bed, they use a drop-down one, so you won't have to go through the hassle of dropping tables and joining benches every day at least twice. This way, you can have your cake and eat it, or in RV terms, have your lounge and bed with almost zero effort.
Execution is very nice, which speaks volumes for the kind of work WildAx does. It adds real, everyday functionality to the build, from the inclusion of a spice rack on the side of the kitchen block to two separate workspace extensions, one attached to the kitchen and the other tucked under the generous fridge.
Photo: WildAx You have a choice between plush upholstery like the one in the demo unit shown below, or you can upgrade to leather for an extra cost. Also for an extra cost, you can expand the standard pack with a 105Ah lithium battery and 240W of solar on the roof, to as much as 340Ah and the complete package that would allow you to go off the grid for longer stretches.
Since you're considering going off the grid, you may also consider going gas free if you want. If you're not new to European motorhomes and campervans, you know that this is not the norm across the entire industry, so WildAx is among those leading the charge.
The bathroom inside the Mercury is as compact as the rest of the RV – and just as nice as well. It comes with a cassette toilet, a shower tray, and a raised bowl sink on a vanity with integrated storage. WildAx uses a rolling door for the entire room, so you won't have to use a curtain when showering.
Photo: WildAx The kitchen is equipped standard with a full-size gas cooktop and oven, and a sink with a separate cover, integrated storage, and the fridge with freezer across the way. WildAx also finds a way to add a full wardrobe, a full mirror, and even more storage in the bedroom space, though those cabinets become completely inaccessible once you lift the bed up into the headliner.
Features include a Truma Combi heater and water heater, a 75-liter (20-gallon) tank for freshwater and a 51-liter (13.5-gallon) one for gray, both winterized, a TV mount, cruise control, cab air conditioning, reversing camera and sensors, alloy wheels, and Truma iNet control screen. The Mercury weighs 2,958 kg (6,521 lbs) empty and has a gross weight of 3,500 kg (7,716 lbs), so you're left with plenty of payload capacity.
Options include the battery and solar upgrade, upgrading to 165 hp and 8-speed automatic transmission, two exterior colors, a TV pack, a two-bike rack, an awning, an external gas outlet, a water filter and tap in the kitchen, microwave, and the upholstery upgrade to leather.
Photo: WildAx These will add to the final price because there's no such thing as a free lunch.
The 2027 WildAx Mercury starts at £70,995 (roughly €84,700 or $95,100 at the current exchange rate), which is affordable in relation to what other premium European manufacturers are charging for slightly bigger variants, after you factor in the extra convenience that comes with a smaller package.

Kia’s electric vehicles could soon be the ones pulling you over. Kia converted the EV5 and PV5 into patrol vehicles as part of its push for greener police cars.
Meet the Kia PV5 and EV5 police vehicle concepts
Electric vehicles make great police cars — they have instant torque, require less maintenance, and are nearly silent.
Several police departments have used electric patrol cars for years, including the Ford Mustang Mach-E and Tesla Model Y.
Kia is eyeing the market with its midsize electric SUV and van. At the 2026 International Public Security Industry Exhibition in South Korea, Kia showcased two patrol vehicle concepts based on the EV5 and PV5.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
The EV5 and PV5 patrol car concepts feature custom lights, sirens, and dedicated police badging on the side.
This year’s theme was “A New Era of K-Public Security by Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Robotics,” so Kia took the opportunity to showcase its latest security equipment and tech.
Kia said the EV5 is a perfect fit for police use, offering “best-in-class” interior space and luggage capacity of up to 965 liters. It features an added luggage board to store equipment and other supplies.
Kia PV5 AI Patrol Car Concept (left) and EV5 Patrol Car Concept (right) Source: Kia
Earlier this year, Kia developed AI patrol cars with the Korean National Police Agency and has been holding training programs to implement electric vehicles.
The AI Patrol Car is based on the PV5, Kia’s 5-seat electric van. The PV5 AI Patrol Vehicle is equipped with three 4K AI cameras and even a drone landing pad mounted on the roof.
The cameras located on the front and rear of the vehicle use AI to detect dangerous situations and automatically alert the driver.
For example, the system can identify guns, knives, bats, and other weapons, as well as emergencies in which someone collapses.
The electric patrol van is equipped with a roof-mounted drone for ground surveillance, while the docking station charges it on the go. The drones have advanced thermal imaging cameras with 90X zoom that can read license plates and pinpoint someone on the run.
Kia’s AI Patrol Cars have been in operation by the Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency’s Wide Area Prevention Patrol Division since last July.
“We intend to showcase the competitiveness of Kia’s electrified mobility and its potential for use as police patrol vehicles,” a Kia official said. The company plans to continue developing custom solutions for police and other public sector use based on its electric vehicles.

NVIDIA OpenShell Reference Architecture
A bit earlier today, NVIDIA kicked off its 2026 GTC Berlin trade show with the event’s lead keynote. Headlined, as always, by CEO Jensen Huang, the GTC Berlin keynote has in recent years become one of NVIDIA’s most important secondary keynotes, as it is the company’s principal trade show for Europe. As the visibility of the GTC Berlin keynote has risen, so has the importance of the show’s announcements.
For their 2026 show, NVIDIA has a mix of hardware and software-related announcements, anchored around AI inference and agentic AI. Of note, NVIDIA is gearing up to put Vera Rubin servers in shipping containers, while on the software side of matters, the company has a slew of updates as well as some new reference architectures for how to use their ever-expanding software ecosystem.
The keynote comes against the backdrop of NVIDIA’s plans for continued growth in Europe. The company has previously said it considers Europe an underserved market and has been eager to expand there. With sovereign AI and new supercomputer builds on the horizon, along with ongoing AI infrastructure build-outs, the company wants to show how European clients are adopting NVIDIA hardware, and why others should too.
DSX POD Puts Vera Rubin NVL72 in a Shipping Container
For hardware news, the highlight of NVIDIA’s 2026 GTC Berlin keynote is the announcement of the DSX POD reference design, a blueprint to build a turnkey Vera Rubin system inside of a container.
NVIDIA GTC Berlin 2026 DSX POD
Not to be confused with NVIDIA’s DGX SuperPOD offerings, which are blueprints to build large DGX system clusters, the DSX POD takes things more literally. It is, in short, a modest multi-rack Vera Rubin system that is built as a fully assembled server container and designed to be transported on-site for installation.
Within the intermodal-sized container (NVIDIA has not confirmed the size, but we suspect it is 40ft), the DSX POD reference design calls for installing seven Vera Rubin NVL72 racks within the container, along with the associated networking, cooling, and management hardware. The resulting containers are not fully self-contained, since they still need to be hooked up to power, networking, and a larger cooling system to run, but beyond utilities, a DSX POD is a fully capable, fully equipped computing system on its own. More likely, multiple PODs will be installed at once to form a larger cluster and quickly fill out a data center, 25 EFLOPs of AI inference at a time. Europe has a history of using modular container-based data center builds.
The containers are fully assembled, tested, and validated at their point of construction. The overarching goal is to further move Vera Rubin system construction from being an on-site activity to something that is done in a factory, with the benefits of scale and quality that come with mass production. A standardized DSX POD, in turn, can be shipped to a site and installed within 14 days, rather than months for an on-site build, ultimately allowing data centers to get their hardware up and running and start making their operators money as soon as possible. Meanwhile, because they use a standard intermodal container size, these PODs can be shipped by truck (as opposed to heavy rail), allowing them to reach virtually anywhere.
NVIDIA GTC Berlin 2026 DSX POD Supporting Hardware
The DSX POD announcement comes as the latest effort from NVIDIA to streamline the installation of NVIDIA’s hardware, following their earlier DSX blueprint announcements. The company’s long-term goal is to keep ramping up hardware sales to hyperscalers and other data centers, and a server-in-a-container is one more tool in its kit. Meanwhile, the fact that they are announcing this at GTC Berlin is not a coincidence, as the European market has become a high priority for NVIDIA as the company eyes upcoming supercomputer builds on the continent and a broader push for sovereign AI. That said, DSX PODs will be available worldwide. This is not a project limited to Europe.
Otherwise, the key point about DSX PODs is that, like NVIDIA’s other DSX blueprints, these are reference designs for NVIDIA’s immediate customers to build. NVIDIA will not build or sell DSX PODs itself. The project’s partner list, in turn, is a general who’s who of hardware vendors, including Gigabyte, HPE, Dell, Delta, QCT, and more. According to NVIDIA, it expects partners to start delivering DSX PODs worldwide in early 2027.
Supply Chain Expansions: From Substrates to Optics
Another key point of Huang’s presentation was an update on NVIDIA’s plans to work with its suppliers to further scale up supply chain capacity over the coming years. NVIDIA has been pushing its partners to the limit for most of the last half-decade, and the company continues to be bottlenecked by supply capacity in one form or another, whether in obvious areas like wafers and memory or in less visible areas such as packaging and testing.
With their latest supply chain push, NVIDIA has set some very lofty goals for its partners. Of note, the company’s plans call for the following capacity improvements over the next three years:
Substrate: 2.5x capacity increase over the next three years, sourced from IBIDEN, Samsung Electro-Mechanics, and Unimiron.
Advanced Packaging: a 4x increase in interposer wafers from Amkor by the end of 2028.
Testing: a 2x capacity increase by 2027 at KYEC.
Co-packaged optics: a whopping 15x increase in capacity of optical engines for co-packaged optics from SIL. And doubling that again to a 30x increase by the end of 2028.
Among these, the optics announcement is especially significant since NVIDIA is moving heavily into co-packaged optics as part of the Vera Rubin generation and beyond. This is a key enabler for allowing for denser networking hardware, and ultimately will be what succeeds large uses of copper networking down the line. NVIDIA’s use of optics is ramping up from relatively small amounts here, which is why there is such a need to ramp things up so heavily.
NVIDIA Co-Packaged Optics
Meanwhile, looping this back around to the target audience at GTC Berlin, these supply chain improvements are intended in part to ramp up NVIDIA’s capacity to supply hardware for AI factory build-outs in Europe. If the company’s plans to grow its sales in Europe are to come to fruition, it will need the capacity to do so.
OpenShell Reference Architecture for Agentic Safety
On the software side, NVIDIA’s GTC Berlin keynote has focused heavily on software, once again underscoring that NVIDIA is, by headcount, a software company first and foremost. Of these announcements, the most significant is arguably the announcement of NVIDIA’s OpenShell reference architecture, which is intended to further flesh out the company’s suite of agentic AI safeties. By providing a blueprint on how to build a safe system around NVIDIA’s hardware and software, NVIDIA is looking to remove some of the friction in building safe agentic AI
NVIDIA GTC Berlin 2026 OpenShell
Like other NVIDIA reference architecture projects, OpenShell is not a new hardware or software project, but a guide on how to best use NVIDIA’s hardware. Specifically, the OpenShell reference architecture builds on its Vera Rubin platform at the hardware level, while the software side leverages its OpenShell secure runtime software, which the company introduced earlier this year.
The reference architecture document , in turn, lays out the rationale and best practices for using OpenShell as part of a complete and secure agentic AI operating environment. NVIDIA’s vision (and marketing pitch) is to use Vera Rubin for the LLM reasoning, Vera CPUs to handle the execution of agents and to run the OpenShell software stack, and finally using BlueField-4 DPUs as the hardware security enforcement mechanism. The reference architecture document, along with the relevant software, is being made available today.
Little Nugget for STH Readers
Several months ago, we did our BIG AI Cluster Little Power the 8x NVIDIA GB10 Cluster .
Since we built that cluster, the NVIDIA GB10s we used have recently doubled in price, and a new NVIDIA DGX Spark 64GB has launched to fill the void. The MikroTik CRS804-4DDQ-hRM that we used has become scarce.
The big news from GTC Berlin is an update to NVIDIA Sync Cluster Assistant. The update will allow DGX Spark to support clusters of up to eight units.
Final Words
NVIDIA’s GTC Berlin keynote comes as the AI boom continues unimpeded, or at least as fast as current supply chains allow. It is no coincidence that one of NVIDIA’s focal points for this year’s keynote is ramping up its supply chains, especially if they intend to facilitate large infrastructure buildouts in Europe. With DSX PODs in tow and a complex software ecosystem to run on top of them, NVIDIA aims to give European providers the tools they need to build and operate their own AI factories, and, in the process, fewer and fewer reasons to say no to NVIDIA.

2027 Honda CBR600RR Supersport Launches With Big Upgrades and Fireblade Tech
70 photos
Photo: Honda
Back in 2024, Japanese bike maker Honda brought back to the European continent a supersport two-wheeler called the CBR600RR. This week, the company presented the latest incarnation of the design, which will be sold as a 2027 model year.
Called by its maker the middleweight supersport jewel, the motorcycle gets enhanced with new looks, performance upgrades, and new technologies meant to allow riders to achieve faster lap times.
The two-wheeler continues to be built around the same frame as before, an aluminum twin-spar design backed by a swingarm made from the same material. The suspension system is made of 41 mm forks at the front and a Pro-Link shock at the rear, both of them supplied by Showa.
The engine that gets this thing going is an inline four-cylinder that displaces 599cc and was tweaked to develop 119 hp at 14,500 rpm and 63 Nm of torque at 11,500 rpm. Power is routed to the back wheel through an assist/slipper clutch and a quickshifter.
There are three standard riding modes on deck for the motorcycle , as well as two custom ones. Finally, a 4-2-1 exhaust system handles the bike's exhaling needs.
For the 2027 model year, Honda adopted for the CBR600RR some tech that's usually deployed on the flagship Fireblade supersport machine. The list includes the radial-mount front brake calipers, the ABS system with three selectable modes, and the electronics package.
Propped on cast aluminum wheels sized 17 inches front and rear, the new CBR600RR carries with it a refreshed look, especially at the front, where Honda opted for a downforce-generating spoiler. When it becomes available at European dealers later on, it will be offered in two color choices, Ignition Red TriColour and Matt Ballistic Black Metallic.
Perhaps the most important news is the fact that the Japanese will make available no less than three Honda Racing Corporation race kits that can only be used on tracks. They all require the removal of all road safety systems and replacing them with things like a racing ECU, racing exhaust, and a revised suspension system.
Adding these kits is understandable, seeing how the CBR600RR is a monster on the track. From more than two decades ago, the motorcycle won the FIM World Super Sports championship for five years in a row in the mid and late 2000s, snatched the Asia Road Racing championship for four years in a row in the 2010s, and the All-Japan Road Race championship at about the same time.
Honda says that since returning to the European market two years ago, it has sold more than 9,600 units of this bike, and that's quite something, seeing how the machine is not meant for everybody. The updates announced this week are, of course, meant to keep the sales numbers going.

The road to the past-producing Crean Hill nickel-copper mine. Credit: Magna Mining
Posted By: Henry Lazenby October 21, 2026
Magna Mining (TSX: NICU; US-OTC: MGMNF) on Tuesday approved construction to start next year at its past-producing Crean Hill project in Ontario, advancing plans to become a three-mine producer in the Sudbury Basin.
A new prefeasibility study, also released Tuesday, estimates initial capital spending of $127 million (US$90.4 million) for 12 years of commercial production. Formal construction at the project, about 350 km northwest of Toronto, is expected to begin in the first half of next year.
“Crean Hill also benefits from a balanced mix of copper, nickel and precious metals production, providing meaningful exposure to seven payable metals without an overreliance on any single commodity,” CEO Jason Jessup said in a release.
The decision adds another development to Magna’s operating McCreedy West mine and Levack restart earlier this month. Desjardins analyst Bryce Adams Wednesday called the update “slightly positive,” saying board approval reduced risk on the path to production. The study’s valuation broadly matched his model, although initial capital was about a third above his $95-million forecast.
Shares gained almost 1% to $2.18 apiece by mid-Wednesday in Toronto, valuing Magna at about $680 million. Adams rates the stock “buy,” with a speculative risk designation and a $5 price target.
$251M value
The base case values Crean Hill at $251 million after tax, using a 7% discount rate, with an internal rate of return of 43%. The estimated 1.5-year payback starts after the three-year construction and ramp-up period.
Those estimates assume copper at US$5.10 per lb., nickel at US$8 per lb. and gold at US$3,600 per oz., alongside platinum at US$1,500 and palladium at US$1,200 per ounce.
During commercial production, annual payable output would average 9.5 million lb. copper, 7.5 million lb. nickel and nearly 42,000 oz. of platinum, palladium and gold combined, according to the study. Precious metals would provide about 39% of revenue.
2030 commercial output
Crean Hill last operated in 2002. Magna acquired the property in 2022 and the revamped project’s first ore sales are expected in late 2027, ahead of commercial production in early 2030. Magna plans to spread initial capital spending over three years, with $33 million next year, $35 million in 2028 and $59 million in 2029.
The company calculates a net initial funding requirement of $72.4 million after $17.2 million in anticipated refundable tax credits and $37.4 million in projected operating cash flow during the ramp-up.
While the construction bill remains the same, Magna’s lower funding estimate assumes it receives expected tax credits and earns as much as forecast from early ore sales.
The company holds cash and equivalents at about $175 million, calculated from Magna’s June balance plus net proceeds from Alpayana’s $140-million equity investment, which closed Aug. 28. The funds support development across Magna’s portfolio.
Magna plans to sell Crean Hill ore to an existing third-party mill in Sudbury. Miners would initially use a new ramp descending from surface, then restore the former No. 2 shaft to hoist ore as workings deepen.

The recurrence of violations at multiple sites led the FDA to conclude that Baxter management must improve its oversight and control of manufacturing.
Baxter has received an FDA warning letter over the shortcomings in its attempts to stop antibiotics from contaminating other drug products.
The FDA issued the warning letter to Baxter’s Round Lake, Illinois, facility after assessing the observations of inspectors who visited the site in March and April. While the letter addresses failings at one plant this spring, the FDA framed the shortcomings as part of broader, longer-term concerns, noting similar violations at the facility in January 2025 and citing related issues at other Baxter plants.
“These repeated failures at multiple sites demonstrate that management oversight and control over the manufacture of drugs is inadequate,” the FDA said.
The Round Lake facility is one of Baxter’s three main pharmaceutical manufacturing plants and the only one on the U.S. mainland. Baxter lists the antibiotics cefazolin, vancomycin and Zosyn among the products manufactured in Round Lake. Cefazolin is a first-generation cephalosporin antibiotic, a type of beta lactam drug that can cause life-threatening allergic reactions.
FDA investigators found Baxter’s facilities and controls were inadequate to prevent conditions that would allow cephalosporin contamination of other drugs, despite a wall separating the parts of the building handling the different products. Baxter considers the wall to be fully sealed and has installed dedicated heating, ventilation and air conditioning units.
Despite those precautions, Baxter’s environmental monitoring program detected cephalosporin in multiple areas on the other side of the building on several occasions since January 2025. The monitoring program was sufficient to identify recurring cross-contamination but inadequate to promptly detect the containment failure, the FDA said.
The site’s inadequacies could cause the underrepresentation of true contamination hazards throughout the facility and create potential for false negative results, the agency added. The FDA is concerned that the quality unit may lack the data needed to make “sound risk-based decisions.”
The cause of the recurring contamination findings remains unclear. Personnel movement is a weakness in the containment strategy but unlikely to be the sole factor contributing to the detected incidents, Baxter told the FDA.
Baxter committed to strengthening investigations into the cephalosporin contamination when the FDA raised its concerns. However, the agency deemed Baxter’s response inadequate because it failed to ensure the complete and comprehensive separation of different parts of the plant. The FDA also scolded the company for failing to thoroughly reevaluate its original risk management decisions.
Cephalosporin contamination was one of four overarching concerns that the FDA raised in its warning letter. The agency also criticized Baxter’s efforts to stop microbiological contamination of drug products and establish laboratory controls for identity, strength, quality and purity.

Mercedes-Benz Promises To Be First To Offer Point-to-Point Driving in Germany, Beating Tesla
10 photos
Photo: Mercedes-Benz
While Tesla is struggling to get FSD approved across Europe, Mercedes-Benz is confident it will be the first to offer point-to-point driving in Germany later this year. This claim is strange unless the German carmaker is certain that Tesla won't get FSD approved this year as it hoped. Earlier this month, Tesla changed FSD name to Tesla Assisted Driving specifically to appease German authorities.
Tesla has been waging a battle with European regulators to get its Full Self-Driving system approved. However, results have been mixed. The automated driving software did receive approval in the Netherlands earlier this year. Other countries followed, with certification based on RDW's (the Dutch regulator) tests.
However, a vote for Europe-wide approval for Tesla FSD was postponed several times, with the next relevant meeting scheduled for December. It appears that other country regulators showed little appetite for approving Elon Musk's driver assistance system. Among key concerns were FSD's misleading name and the software's disregard for speed limits.
Tesla engaged in discussions with Germany's Ministry of Transport (BMV) and agreed to address these issues. It immediately changed the FSD name in Europe to the more benign Tesla Assisted Driving (TAD), and placed a cap on the software's speed offset at 10% above the posted speed limit. In light of the changes, Federal Transport Minister Steffen Bilger said that he would advocate for TAD approval across Europe "as quickly as possible."
I would've expected that Germany would've quickly approved TAD nationwide based on RDW's certification. After all, Lithuania, Estonia, Denmark, Belgium, Slovenia, Czech Republic, Croatia, and Slovakia did just that. It turns out that Germany, which is the home country of heavyweights like Volkswagen, BMW, and Mercedes-Benz, has no intention of letting Tesla steal the show at home.
Photo: Mercedes-Benz This is now crystal clear, as Mercedes-Benz announced that it would be the first to offer point-to-point assisted driving in Germany. The carmaker will start an early access program later this year in Stuttgart and Munich. Regular customers will be able to join from early 2027. Mercedes-Benz says that its MB.Drive Assist Pro has been developed according to the latest UNECE regulations and doesn't need further regulatory approval.
MB.Drive Assist Pro combines the MB.OS operating system with the Nvidia Hyperion computers and sensors and Alpamayo Stack software to enable automated driving features. Although this should be capable of driving without human intervention, Mercedes-Benz still markets it as an advanced SAE Level-2 system, which requires continuous driver supervision.
MB.Drive Assist Pro was introduced last year on the 2026 Mercedes-Benz CLA EV and quickly expanded to the 2027 GLB, GLC EV, C-Class EV, and other MY2027 models. Developed in partnership with Nvidia, the system is set to power a wide range of Mercedes-Benz's car and van models. MB.Drive Assist Pro can navigate heavy city traffic, including traffic lights and lane changes under the driver's supervision.

source_document.body:
News
Crews lift and install the first major structural truss for the first fab at Intel’s Ohio One site in New Albany. (Credit: Intel Corporation)
Intel has reached a visible construction milestone at its Ohio One site in New Albany, Ohio, with the installation of the first major structural truss for the company’s first fab on the campus. Coincidentally, this is not too far (30 minutes) from where the recent Patrick and Jeff Geerling at Micro Center Columbus, Ohio happened. We saw this photo as part of an Intel release around construction and tool installation in Arizona for Fab 62, and a commitment to US manufacturing at other sites like Oregon and New Mexico, but this just seemed cool so we decided to do something a bit different for that announcement since we had not covered the truss installation.
Intel’s Ohio One US Manufacturing Push
The Ohio One project was announced in January 2022 , with Intel saying production would start in 2025. The 1,000-acre site east of Columbus was part of a broader plan to expand domestic manufacturing capacity using state and federal funding alongside Intel’s capital investment.
A Rendering Shows Early Plans For Two New Leading Edge Intel Pro
Intel’s US expansion received significant federal backing through the CHIPS Act. In March 2024, Intel and the White House announced a preliminary memorandum of terms for up to $8.5 billion in direct funding , along with investment tax credits and low-interest loans, to support fab construction across Arizona, New Mexico, Ohio, and Oregon. Intel and the White House said the funding was expected to create around 10,000 Intel jobs and another 20,000 in the construction sector.
Intel continues construction on its sixth high-volume manufacturing facility at Fab 62 in Arizona, near STH. That site, like Ohio One, represents a long-term bet on US-based leading-edge production.
Intel’s Fab 62 in Arizona
Intel says that Fab 62 is still under construction but tool installation has begun.
Intel Chandler Fabs From The Fields Large
Intel Foundry’s broader strategy has evolved since those early announcements. In September 2024, Intel restructured its foundry business into an independent subsidiary and announced a multi-year deal with AWS to produce custom chips on Intel 18A. The company also paused projects in Poland and Germany by approximately two years, citing market demand, while reaffirming commitment to US sites including Ohio. That was due to a capital crunch, but demand for semiconductors on leading process nodes is clearly very healthy these days.
Intel’s image from the Truss announcement
Construction timelines have shifted since the initial announcement. In a February 2025 report to the Ohio Department of Development, Intel stated it was adjusting its anticipated schedule for the two Ohio fabs. The company projected completing construction of the first fab in 2030 and beginning operations in 2030-2031, with the second fab expected to complete construction in 2031 and begin operations in 2032.
Final Words
The truss installation at Ohio One shows that Intel’s US manufacturing expansion remains active despite financial pressures and strategic pivots. For readers tracking the foundry business, this is still early days. The company needs to complete the shells, install and calibrate equipment, and start running wafers, which are all non-trivial steps. Still, it is at least some progress on the Ohio campus. Arizona fab tool installation and progress are also a good sign since it means Intel will hopefully bring more wafer volume online when it plans to begin operations by the end of 2028. New Mexico packaging is seen as a big growth driver for Foundry. Oregon is getting the research investment. Even in Santa Clara, California, Intel recently broke ground on a mask manufacturing facility. Intel has a lot going on on the Foundry side. Now let us see if they can build fabs that customers fill fast enough.

Financial distress continues to affect trucking companies across the U.S., with at least 16 carriers filing for bankruptcy protection between Sept. 18 and Oct. 21.
According to a FreightWaves review of federal bankruptcy records, the filings span multiple freight segments, including general freight, petroleum transportation, logging and timber hauling. They also involve companies ranging from single-truck operators to carriers reporting dozens of power units.
The bankruptcies include both Chapter 7 liquidation cases and Chapter 11 proceedings, which generally allow businesses to restructure debts while potentially continuing operations.
Among the larger carriers identified in the review are Illinois-based Georgia-based KLS Logging Inc., which lists 53 power units and 28 drivers; and McAllen, Texas-based American Petroleum Carriers, which filed for Chapter 11 protection. The company lists 16 trucks and 10 drivers.
The filings highlight financial challenges confronting smaller trucking businesses.
Illinois carrier lists $2.3 million in liabilities
Chicago-based Midwest Expedited Co. filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection Oct. 6 in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Northern District of Illinois.
The company, which lists 95 trucks on its LinkedIn page but seven Freightliner trucks specifically identified in its bankruptcy schedules, reported approximately $2.31 million in liabilities against just $108,351 in assets, according to its bankruptcy schedules.
The filing lists $935,384 in secured claims and approximately $1.38 million in nonpriority unsecured claims.
Midwest Expedited’s bankruptcy schedules identify seven Freightliner M2 trucks from the 2023 and 2024 model years, collectively valued at $107,500. The seven vehicles listed in court documents are not necessarily representative of the company’s previously reported fleet size.
Texas carrier reports sharp revenue decline
In El Paso, Texas, Site2Site Transport filed for Chapter 7 bankruptcy protection Sept. 29 after reporting a substantial decline in annual revenue.
According to its bankruptcy filing, the company generated approximately $2.1 million in gross revenue in 2024, compared with $1.6 million in 2025 — a decline of roughly 24%.
The filing reported no gross revenue from Jan. 1, 2026, through the bankruptcy filing date.
Site2Site also disclosed leases involving eight trucks and liabilities exceeding $493,000.
The Chapter 7 filing indicates the company is pursuing liquidation rather than a traditional Chapter 11 restructuring.
Another Texas carrier, McAllen-based American Petroleum Carriers, filed for Chapter 11 protection in the Southern District of Texas under case number 26-70331.
The company lists 16 trucks and 10 drivers.
Bankruptcy filings extend across multiple states
Other filings illustrate how bankruptcy proceedings are affecting trucking operations of different sizes.
KLS Logging Inc., based in Lyons, Georgia, filed for Chapter 11 protection in the Southern District of Georgia.
Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration information included in the review identifies the company as operating 53 power units with 28 registered drivers. The carrier primarily transports unmanufactured logs, poles, beams and lumber.
In Oregon, Lakeview-based Eskil Trucking filed for Chapter 11 protection after reporting more than $1 million in liabilities and no more than $500,000 in assets.
The company previously reported seven trucks and six drivers. Its bankruptcy filing identified nearly $855,000 owed to Sargent Transportation, another southern Oregon trucking company, as its largest creditor claim.
Several Illinois-based transportation businesses also sought bankruptcy protection.
Maksteel Transport LLC filed Chapter 11 on Sept. 23, listing five trucks and three drivers. Douglass Logistics LLC filed Chapter 11 the same day, reporting 15 trucks and 10 drivers.
Windy City Supply Chain LLC filed Chapter 7 on Oct. 2. The company listed 20 owner-operator drivers, although the number of trucks it owned or operated was not established in the information reviewed.
Lake Zurich-based Xcalibur Logistics, which lists one truck and one driver, also filed for Chapter 7 protection.
In North Carolina, FAB Trucking LLC filed Chapter 11 in the Eastern District of North Carolina, while High Point-based Porter’s Hauling LLC filed Chapter 7. Another High Point carrier, Queen’s Hauling LLC, was identified in bankruptcy records, although the chapter was not established in the available research.
Additional filings involved Wooten 4 Trucking LLC in Illinois, Jotham Trucking LLC in Michigan, Tros Logging in Alabama and Gerek Trucking in West Virginia.

Kodiak Copper CEO Claudia Tornquist last month at the Precious Metals Summit in Beaver Creek, Colo.
Posted By: Henry Lazenby October 21, 2026
Kodiak Copper (TSXV: KDK; US-OTC: KDKCF) is targeting a larger resource at its MPD copper-gold project in southern B.C. by March, CEO Claudia Tornquist says.
Recent drilling at the Ketchan deposit returned 283.5 metres grading 0.56% copper and 0.15 gram gold per tonne from 37.5 metres downhole, the company reported Sept. 9. The hole filled a gap in the existing resource model.
“And our focus, of course, in particular, is on near-surface mineralization and on high-grade mineralization, because that is what will be important as we move into economic evaluation,” Tornquist told The Northern Miner late last month at the Precious Metals Summit in Beaver Creek, Colo.
The planned 16,500-metre drill program aims to show growth potential of MPD’s seven deposits while testing additional exploration targets. For Kodiak, the challenge is to establish both the scale and grade needed to support a conceptual starter mine.

source_document.body:
Lucid’s European robotaxi deal now has a driver. Bolt announced today that its fleet of at least 25,000 autonomous Lucid vehicles will run Nvidia’s Alpamayo Stack self-driving software, starting with a data-collection program in Madrid in 2027.
That gives Lucid two robotaxi customers on two different autonomy systems: Nuro’s software for Uber’s Gravity robotaxis in the US, and now Nvidia’s for Bolt in Europe.
The piece missing from September
When Lucid and Bolt announced the 25,000-vehicle deal last month, nobody said who would write the driving software. The vehicles were to be built around Nvidia Hyperion, a reference design for compute and sensors, which isn’t a self-driving system on its own. Bolt said it would bring in autonomous-driving partners later.
It picked Nvidia again. Alpamayo Stack is Nvidia’s full-stack driving software, which the company describes as “reasoning AI” combined with classical perception and planning, running on Hyperion with its Halos safety tools on top. The two will tune the software for European driving, and Lucid is only the first automaker Bolt plans to put it in.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
Madrid comes first, in 2027. The cars there won’t carry riders at the start. Their job is to collect real-world driving data so Bolt and Nvidia can develop and validate the software, and even that still needs regulatory approval. Germany and France are named as the next key markets.
Jevgeni Kabanov, Bolt’s president and head of autonomous driving, said the Region of Madrid is “pioneering a structured framework for commercial autonomous mobility.” On Lucid’s side, the work runs through Lucid Technologies. Its president, Kay Stepper, called the “launch of data collection next year” one of “the first steps” toward autonomous mobility in Europe.
Which Lucid, and when?
Bolt didn’t say which Lucid model goes to Madrid.
The September deal was designed around Lucid’s upcoming Midsize platform, the same platform whose first vehicle, the Cosmos, got pushed to 2027 in Lucid’s August operating reset, “most likely the second half.” If the purpose-built vehicle isn’t ready in time, Madrid’s first data-collection cars would have to be existing Gravity or Air vehicles.
There’s also no date for anyone riding without a driver. Data collection is step one.
Lucid’s robotaxi math
Add up both programs and Lucid has a lot of robotaxis on order, at least on paper. Uber’s program with Lucid and Nuro now calls for at least 35,000 Gravity vehicles globally, up from Uber’s original commitment to 20,000 . Bolt adds at least 25,000. That’s 60,000 vehicles.
For scale, Lucid delivered 15,841 vehicles in all of 2025 and 10,852 in the first nine months of 2026. Those robotaxi commitments equal almost four years of Lucid’s current deliveries.
The Uber program is further along, but it isn’t open to the public yet. Uber employees have been taking test rides in Gravity robotaxis in San Francisco since April, with a safety operator behind the wheel. The public Bay Area launch is still promised for 2026, with Houston to follow in mid-2027.
Bolt is also hedging. It runs a separate track with Pony.ai and Stellantis, which announced a pilot in Luxembourg in June, and it’s targeting 100,000 autonomous vehicles on its platform across Europe and the wider UNECE region by 2035.
As for Nvidia, it has spent years selling chips and sensor reference designs to automakers. With Alpamayo Stack, it’s now selling the driver too, which puts it up against Nuro, Waymo, and Tesla’s software.

Intramotev will deploy two autonomous freight railcars on Missouri’s Columbia Terminal Railroad as part of a project supported by a $16.2 million federal grant awarded to the City of Columbia.
The Federal Railroad Administration selected the city for funding under its Consolidated Rail Infrastructure and Safety Improvements (CRISI) program, according to the announcement. Intramotev will serve as the technology partner, deploying its TugVolt technology on COLT’s 21.4-mile line between Centralia and Columbia.
Operations will proceed in phases under an FRA-approved test program, beginning with remote switching at COLT’s Columbia terminal and advancing to autonomous freight service across the full mainline, including its public crossings. The grant also will fund track and infrastructure upgrades.
“Short lines keep America’s small cities and rural communities connected to the freight network,” said Tim Luchini, Intramotev’s chief executive. “Autonomous railcars can help them serve more customers, more often, at lower cost, and this program will show what that looks like on a working mainline.”
COLT is a municipally owned short line operated by Columbia City Utilities. Intramotev will build both TugVolt units at its St. Louis facility.
“COLT has been Columbia’s link to the national rail network for nearly 40 years, and the businesses that depend on it support hundreds of local jobs,” said Erin Keys, the city’s utilities director. “This federal investment lets us modernize the railroad, strengthen service for our customers, and put Columbia at the forefront of rail innovation.”
The project is intended to produce a safety record that FRA and the more than 600 U.S. short-line railroads can use as a template for adopting autonomous railcars, according to the announcement. It did not specify a deployment date or a timetable for moving from terminal switching to full-line service.
The award follows other developments for Intramotev this year. In April, the company announced an agreement with Austria’s OBB Rail Cargo Group. In June, U.S. Army Reserve soldiers trained on TugVolt technology during a planned technology assessment.

Lexus announced prices for its first fully electric three-row SUV, the 2027 TZ, with sales set to begin in the US later this year and in Europe in early 2027.
2027 Lexus TZ prices and range
The new TZ is the largest, most luxurious Lexus electric SUV to date. It will go on sale by the end of 2026 in the US, and early 2027 in Europe.
In the US, the 2027 Lexus TZ will be available in three trims, starting at $64,050. The base TZ 450e Premium AWD model will be available to order in late 2026, followed by the Premium Touring AWD and Luxury AWD trims in early 2027.
The three-row electric SUV will be available with two battery packs: 76.96 kWh and 95.82 kWh. The former provides an EPA-estimated range of up to 253 miles, while the latter gets up to 315 miles.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
All TZ variants come with an evolved version of Lexus’ DIRECT4 AWD system. The dual-motor AWD setup delivers a combined 308 horsepower.
2027 Lexus TZ interior (Source: Lexus)
Inside, the three-row electric SUV features the latest Lexus Interface multimedia system. The setup includes a 14″ multimedia touchscreen display with customizable widgets, a Voice Assistant, and full-screen navigation on the digital cluster.
The 2027 Lexus TZ is 200.8″ long, 78.3″ wide, and 67.1″ tall, with a 120.1″ wheelbase, or roughly the same size as the Hyundai IONIQ 9 and the Volvo EX90.
2027 Lexus TZ (Source: Lexus)
The base 2027 Lexus TZ 450e Premium AWD will be available to order later this year, starting at $64,050 with up to 253 miles of range.
In early 2027, the Touring and Luxury models will go on sale, starting at $72,050 and $80,550, respectively. Both use the extended-range 95.82 kWh battery. The Touring model offers up to 315 miles of range, while the most expensive Luxury trim gets 279 miles.

Lexus said the electric SUV can recharge from 10% to 80% in about 35 minutes at up to 150 kW. It also includes an NACS charge port so you can access Tesla Superchargers without a separate adapter.
Lexus revealed TZ prices in several European markets ahead of its official market launch in early 2027.
2027 Lexus TZ prices in the Netherlands (Source: Lexus Netherlands)
In the Netherlands , it will be available in three variants: 450e Standard Range, 450e Long Range Executive Line, and 450e Long Range President Line.
The base Standard Range model starts at 79,995 euros ($90,000), including a limited-time 4,000 euro discount.
2027 Lexus TZ 550e interior (Source: Lexus UK)
It uses the same 77 kWh and 95.8 kWh batteries, offering a WLTP range of up to 280 miles (450 km) and 338 miles (544 km), respectively.
In Spain, the 2027 Lexus TZ will go on sale starting at 88,000 euros ($99,000), with prices ranging up to 105,000 euros ($118,000) for the top-spec Luxury two-tone variant.

Photo: SH Proshots
This prototype of the redesigned X7 makes a particularly emphatic statement. Not only does it come with M Yellow Lights inspired by the Bavarian automaker's endurance racing programs, but four exhaust pipes further mean the 4.4-liter S68 engine is also featured.
Previously restricted to special editions like the M4 CS, yellow daytime running lights recently expanded to series-production models like the M350 xDrive, X5 M60, and the X5 M60e. Lesser versions of the 3 Series and X5 use white DRLs instead. But why did BMW decide on yellow for these particular models?
You can thank endurance racing and physics for that. Yellow light has longer wavelengths, meaning that less glare is created when reflecting off mist, fog, rain, or dust. Yellow further improves depth perception and contrast during night stints, namely the stints where the big errors are usually made in endurance racing.
The motorsport connection is not singular, though. French cars used yellow headlights from the 1930s all the way until the 1990s for better performance in bad weather. In real-world driving scenarios, yellow glass or bulb coatings filter out the shorter wavelengths of light, decreasing glare during night driving.
Out back, we can see this X7 M60 xDrive packing thin and stacked horizontal taillights. Due to camouflage wrap, it's hard to determine if the slim taillight clusters are connected by a full-width light bar. Their lighting signature, however, mirrors that of the iX7 our spy photographers recently spotted at the Ring.
Photo: SH Proshots Gifted with a slightly more aggressive rear bumper due to the quad exhaust setup, the X7 continues with split headlights. Just like the iX7 , which uses the same codename as the next generation of the X7, the main headlamps feature lower separate housings. The daytime running lights are very slim, located on either side of the nose, where the front bumper meets the hood and front quarter panels.
Equipped with larger wheels and brake calipers than the recently spied iX7, the X7 in M60 xDrive specification doesn't have pull-up door handles. A quarter of small winglets are featured, and this design is certain to be changed to pull-up handles in China. Under standard GB 48001-2026, automakers are required to offer a hand-operable gripping recess of at least 60 by 20 by 25 millimeters.
Not chasing the X6's sloping coupe-inspired proportions, the boxy X7 should make in excess of 500 horsepower when optioned with the S68 engine. For reference, the outgoing M60 xDrive develops 523 hp and 553 lb-ft (750 Nm) with premium-grade dinosaur brew in the fuel tank. Modest bumps are likely, and the emphasis falls on 'modest' due to Euro 7 regulations on the Old Continent.
As ever, an 8-speed automatic from ZF should be the only transmission available, regardless of engine. Instead of a full-on M version of the 2028 model year X7, the G67 will gain a bunch of Alpina versions. Codenamed G69, the Alpina range is expected to include the X7 40 xDrive, X7 60 xDrive, and iX7 100 xDrive.
Alpina models are said to default to 6 seats. Production, meanwhile, should kick off at the Spartanburg plant in the US at some point in September 2027.
